quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Allows you to sit far enough forward that your arms will be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Allows you to sit as far back as possible and have to stretch when trying to reach the handle grips.
Makes you lean over the bike, requiring your arms to hold you up.
Allows for your knees to be kept far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to sit far enough forward that your arms will be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit far enough forward so your arms are slightly bent when you hold the handle grips. This helps you reach and control all the motorcycle's controls easily.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means that:

options.text: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
The alcohol never gets removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Once it is in your system, your body gets rid of the alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Any gear that helps to protect you.
The lowest-priced gear.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps to protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Polyester.
Silk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong, durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
A patch of leaves
An ice patch
Dry concrete

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Gravel, leaves, ice, wet pavement, mud, snow, painted lines, and metal covers can be slippery for motorcycles. Dry concrete provides good traction.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.

questions.question: Of the following, which clothing item will not reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only at night.
Be worn only during the day.
Not be worn.
Be worn day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing at all times. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright colors during daylight too.

questions.question: The single most effective thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving an accident is:

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Read books on motorcycle safety.
Ask others about how to ride more safely.
Watch training videos.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle riding clothing?

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can provide protection in the event of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can provide protection in the event of a crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly but still allow you to move freely.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider be ready for when passing parked cars?

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A motorist to unexpectedly pull out of a parking space and into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other motorists to see the motorcycle and stay out of its way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorist to unexpectedly pull out of a parking space and into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic. Ride on the left side of your lane to create more space between you and parked cars.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close to the motorcycle.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals every time you change lanes or turn, even if you don't see other vehicles nearby. This is especially important because motorcycles are small and vulnerable.

questions.question: How can you make night riding safer?

options.text: Is discouraged.
Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Have only a front brake.
Have only a rear brake.
Have brakes in both the front and rear.
Have three brakes: one in the front, one in the rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver cannot see you if you ride in their blind spot. This is dangerous because the vehicle could change lanes into you or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders be careful about when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.
Cars leaving their parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars leaving their parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, watch for cars pulling away from the curb or leaving parking spaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no visible damage, like cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly around your entire head, and have no visible damage like cracks or loose padding. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Is not important.
Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal driving routine.
Does not help since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal driving routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal driving. Also check them before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Get a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Get a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Get a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Get a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, you will lose all power to the rear wheel right away.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you stuck in one area of the lane with no room to move.
Means you can rely on other drivers to spot hazards.
Requires you to drive faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle on all sides. This gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to drift into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you start to turn.
